primary_edition.title: Les plus anciens monuments du christianisme, second part; Hamburg fragment F
primary_edition.source_type: printed primary transcription and apparatus, not original parchment photograph
primary_edition.description: Printed479 calls it a parchment codex leaf,156x125mm with117x92mm writing; IV/Vcentury; first edition Schmidt/Schubart Berlin1909XLIIpp1077–1081.

method: Direct bounded visual reading, including enlarged faded print. No photo authentication, no fresh1909 scan collation and no exhaustive manuscript certification. Printed abbreviation expansions and dots are editorial evidence, not an unqualified claim of preserved letters.

excerpts.finding: Contains IV.6negative receive-nothing tail, shorter IV.7 and IV.8 fruit promise. The away-from-Lord/pure-mind stretch is absent in this printed recto, confirming the previously Bonner-reported Hamburg omission. IV.8 has future ability. The catalogue’s4.6–7 description is not used as an exact exclusion of the physically printed fruit-promise text.

Contains I.1–2 and I.3–5 opening. Heading numeration differs and does not reorder the project reader. Verso10–12 prints Hermas’s Yes/sir/happy-if-I-learn-the-acceptable-fast reply, with the final divine abbreviation printed without Michigan’s missing-theta brackets. This directly consulted edition corroborates the earlier restored reply; it is not a new additional source locus or a second Hamburg witness.

Reports the reply absent Athos/Vulgata/Ethiopic and its opening in Palatina. The Palatina version was directly checked in the previous fasting repair; this Wessely report alone does not certify a newly read Ethiopic manuscript.
Retains I.4to-God wording and contrasts BUTserve with reported AthosAND. Printed divine abbreviations are expanded for sense only; exact damaged letters are not treated as uniformly legible.
